newsitem.title: CHINA: China hails second full year of air safety.
newsitem.headline: China hails second full year of air safety.

text.p: Chinese authorities hailed on Thursday the end of a second whole year without an aviation disaster after several years in which China became one of the world's most dangerous places in which to fly.

"Despite frequent disasters in other parts of the world last year, China's aviation sector set a record of 29 months, and 2.33 million hours, of safe flying," the China Daily quoted Bao Peide, deputy director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), as saying.
Bao issued the statement after China's last international flight of the year, an Air China airliner from Sydney to Beijing, touched down safely just before midnight on Monday.
In 1994, the International Airline Passenger Association cited China as one of the most dangerous places in the world in which to fly after a string of crashes and hijackings.

China's civil aviation sector has expanded rapidly in the past 16 years, growing by an average of 20.6 percent between 1980 and 1995. It was forecast to grow 14 percent annually through the end of the century.
